row.evidence: Parse.ly's SSO docs say: "Parse.ly does not support Just-in-Time (JIT) or System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) provisioning."
row.notes: No public prices: the pricing page lists Content Performance, Content Value and Content Advocacy tiers with no prices (book a demo). SAML 2.0 SSO (Okta, OneLogin or any SAML IdP) and Google-enforced sign-in appear on the Content Advocacy tier and must be purchased; SSO only controls sign-in for users who already exist, since Parse.ly states it supports neither JIT nor SCIM. Users are invited, edited and removed by admins in the dashboard, with CSV export of users. The Parse.ly API is an analytics add-on with no documented user-management endpoints. The Okta OIN Parse.ly app is SWA only.

limitations.text: SSO requires existing Parse.ly Dash accounts; no JIT or SCIM provisioning.

user_api.notes: The Parse.ly API (an add-on) is an analytics API keyed by Site ID and API secret; no user, role or licence endpoints are documented. User management is in the dashboard only.

okta.notes: OIN Parse.ly app shows only SWA ticked (read from page markup); last updated Sep 2021.

fallbacks.notes: Admins invite users by email (comma-separated, several at once) and can export users as CSV; no CSV import documented.
